question: What are the key components of Angular?
answer:
Components define view + behavior units, while directives attach reusable behavior to existing elements. This split helps teams avoid large monolithic components.

When comparing them, explain intent: components render screens; directives modify or extend DOM behavior without owning a full view.

question: What are Angular elements?
answer:
Angular Elements lets Angular components be packaged as browser-standard custom elements. This enables sharing UI widgets across Angular and non-Angular hosts.

Inputs and outputs map to element properties and DOM events, so integration works through standard web APIs.

examples.title: Register Angular custom element
examples.code:
const widget = createCustomElement(WidgetComponent, { injector });
customElements.define("app-widget", widget);
examples.explanation: Registers an Angular component as a browser custom element.

tip: Document each input/output mapping so non-Angular consumers can integrate safely.

question: What are different types of compilation in Angular?
answer:
Angular compilation converts templates and decorators into executable instructions. Build-time compilation catches errors earlier and reduces runtime compiler work.

Most production pipelines use strict compiler settings to fail fast on template and metadata issues before deployment.

examples.explanation: Compile-time checks catch template issues before deployment.

tip: Enable strict template checks in CI to catch compiler issues before release.

question: What is zone?
answer:
Zone.js patches asynchronous browser APIs so Angular can trigger change detection after async work completes. This is why UI updates happen after timers, HTTP calls, or events without manual refresh steps.

Understanding zones helps optimize performance: run noisy non-UI tasks outside Angular zone and re-enter only when state changes affect the view.

examples.explanation: Avoids extra change detection for high-frequency browser events.

tip: Use `runOutsideAngular` for noisy async work, then re-enter only when UI state changes.
